summary: Penn Valley Airport is a small general aviation facility serving Selinsgrove and the surrounding Susquehanna Valley in central Pennsylvania. Jointly owned by Selinsgrove Borough and Snyder County, the airport features a single asphalt runway and supports recreational flying, flight training, and business aviation. Its convenient location near US Route 11 and US Route 15 makes it a practical gateway to the scenic heart of Pennsylvania.
faqs:
Q: What is Penn Valley Airport primarily used for?
A: Penn Valley Airport primarily serves general aviation, including private flights, flight training, recreational flying, and occasional business aviation. It does not host scheduled commercial airline service.

Q: How long is the runway at KSEG?
A: The airport features a single asphalt runway (Runway 17/35) approximately 4,800 feet in length, suitable for most single-engine and light twin-engine aircraft.

Q: Are there rental cars available at the airport?
A: Rental car availability is limited; visitors are encouraged to arrange ground transportation in advance with local providers in Selinsgrove.

Q: Is there an air traffic control tower at Penn Valley Airport?
A: No, KSEG is an uncontrolled airport. Pilots communicate on the common traffic advisory frequency (CTAF) to coordinate arrivals and departures.
transport_tips: The airport is located just off US Route 11/15, making it a quick drive from downtown Selinsgrove, Sunbury, and Lewisburg. Ground transportation options are limited, so arranging a rental car or pre-booked ride in advance is recommended. Ample free parking is available on-site for those picking up or dropping off passengers.
local_tip: If you have time before or after your flight, take a short drive into downtown Selinsgrove for a meal at one of the locally owned restaurants along Market Street — the small-town Pennsylvania hospitality is a highlight of visiting the Susquehanna Valley.
